prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single PORTRAIT 9:16 image, 1080x1920 or the highest actually supported native portrait resolution close to 9:16. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 70% of width and central 70% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 18.49. Exact Sanskrit: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः ।
नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥ ४९ ॥ Exact stored meaning: One whose intellect is unattached everywhere, whose self is conquered, from whom all longing has departed — through renunciation, that one attains the supreme perfection of non-action (naiṣkarmya). Chapter context: Renunciation, duties, knowledge/action/agency, understanding, resolve, joy, surrender and the closing dialogue. Follow the exact verse-specific teaching; bring Sanjaya and Dhritarashtra back into the palace for the closing narration when appropriate. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: O Kaunteya, one should not abandon the duty born of one's own nature, even if it is flawed; for all undertakings are covered by imperfection as fire is covered by smoke. Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: O Kaunteya, hear from me briefly how one who has attained perfection reaches Brahman — that is the highest culmination of knowledge. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene. Phone-first composition update, owner 2026-10-19: phones are the primary reading device, tablets secondary. Keep the complete meaningful scene compact and intelligible at 320–430 logical pixels wide. Arrange the important relationships as one close, coherent central grouping; avoid essential tiny distant figures and wide edge-to-edge action. Keep generous quiet margins on all four sides, no faces, hands, feet, narrative objects or important background subjects touching the frame. The complete portrait painting will be contained inside the phone reading area, never stretched or cropped to fill it; do not depend on edge cropping. Preserve the approved watercolor style and the exact verse meaning. No labels, letters, sacred syllables, explanatory marks or typography. Portrait-format owner update 2026-10-19: create a genuinely tall 9:16 painted composition for phone reading, not a square painting pasted on blank portrait paper. The atmosphere and natural scene should continue organically through the portrait canvas. Keep all important subjects wholly visible, inside quiet margins; no frame-edge clipping. Use one coherent compact narrative group, with detail readable on a phone. This same portrait painting is reused proportionally on tablets and landscape screens; do not create a second image for tablets.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 18.49: One whose intellect is unattached everywhere, whose self is conquered, from whom all longing has departed — through renunciation, that one attains the supreme perfection of non-action (naiṣkarmya).
